description: 25 AI transformation anti-patterns organized into 5 domains. High scores indicate presence of harmful patterns.

criteria.title: AI Decision Fog & Governance Fat
criteria.description: AI decisions stall or repeat across forums because ownership, decision rights, and escalation boundaries are unclear.
sub_criteria: Are AI initiatives delayed because nobody clearly owns decisions?
Do separate governance forums create repeated approvals instead of enabling flow?
Are teams forced to escalate ordinary AI design decisions to senior leaders because decision boundaries are unclear?

criteria.title: One-Size-Fits-All AI Delivery
criteria.description: All AI initiatives are forced through the same delivery model regardless of uncertainty, risk, demand type, or learning need.
sub_criteria: Are all AI initiatives forced through the same project model regardless of uncertainty?
Are exploratory AI cases managed with rigid delivery plans that assume known requirements?
Are predictable automation cases mixed with uncertain GenAI or agentic work in the same backlog without routing logic?

criteria.title: Pilot Purgatory
criteria.description: AI pilots remain disconnected from production, service-area ownership, safety evidence, reusable platform capabilities, and measurable business outcomes.
sub_criteria: Do AI pilots remain disconnected from production, service-area ownership, or value outcomes?
Are pilots considered successful without proving integration, safety, adoption, learning, or measurable business value?
Does every new AI use case start from scratch instead of reusing learnings, pilot playbooks, patterns, and platform capabilities?

criteria.title: Fragmented AI Knowledge & Hero Culture
criteria.description: AI knowledge is concentrated in isolated experts, repeated mistakes, and heroics instead of reusable institutional learning.
sub_criteria: Is AI knowledge concentrated in a few experts or isolated data science teams?
Are mistakes repeated because learning is not institutionalized?
Do teams depend on individual heroes instead of shared practices, reusable playbooks, and operating structures?

criteria.title: Digital Taylorism & Workslop
criteria.description: AI accelerates fragmented tasks but increases rework, checking, coordination, cognitive load, or low-quality output.
sub_criteria: Is AI used mainly to make fragmented tasks faster without improving the whole system?
Does AI create extra checking, rework, hidden coordination, or low-quality workslop?
Are people measured on activity and utilization rather than impact, learning, quality, and customer value?

criteria.title: Legacy Labyrinth & Brittle AI Connectivity
criteria.description: AI use cases depend on manual exports, screen scraping, brittle brownfield point integrations, unclear service boundaries, and fragile dependencies.
sub_criteria: Do AI use cases depend on manual exports, screen scraping, copied files, or fragile custom connectors?
Does touching one legacy or brownfield system break another because service boundaries are unclear?
Are AI integrations created project-by-project with no reusable architecture?

criteria.title: Notebook-to-Production / Prompt-to-Production Chaos
criteria.description: Models, prompts, and agents move into production without versioning, review, reproducibility, or rollback.
sub_criteria: Are models, prompts, or agents moved into production without repeatable release controls?
Are prompt changes made manually without versioning, review, or rollback?
Is it impossible to reproduce why an AI system behaved a certain way?

criteria.title: Black-Box AI Operations
criteria.description: AI failures, static-model drift, hallucinations, retrieval degradation, value erosion, and unsafe outputs are found through complaints rather than Sense & Respond monitoring.
sub_criteria: Are AI failures discovered mainly through user complaints or business damage?
Are there no baseline metrics for accuracy, first-time-right, value, safety, or operational reliability?
Are model drift, retrieval degradation, hallucinations, unsafe outputs, or value degradation not systematically detected?

criteria.title: Safety Theater & Unbounded Autonomy
criteria.description: Guardrails are trusted without red-team evidence, agents have unclear behavioral limits, and safety reviews happen too late.
sub_criteria: Are AI systems trusted because guardrails exist without evidence of testing?
Can agents access tools, systems, or data without clear behavioral boundaries or Human-in-the-Loop escalation paths?
Are safety reviews performed as late-stage gates instead of Secure-by-Design controls built into service design?

criteria.title: Tool Fragmentation & Hidden Factory
criteria.description: Every AI project assembles its own stack, tools, governance, monitoring, and maintenance burden without shared standards.
sub_criteria: Does every AI project build its own ingestion, governance, hosting, evaluation, and monitoring stack?
Are teams buying disconnected tools without common standards, cost controls, or observability?
Does platform fragmentation create maintenance debt and reduce innovation capacity?

criteria.title: AI Slogan Strategy
criteria.description: AI is treated as a generic transformation slogan without strategic choices, value boundaries, or prioritization logic.
sub_criteria: Is AI described as a generic transformation theme without clear strategic choices?
Is everything labeled as an AI priority without prioritization logic?
Are AI tools adopted before the organization knows what value it wants to create?

criteria.title: Use-Case Chasing & Vanity Benefits
criteria.description: AI initiatives are selected for visibility, fashion, tool adoption, or cost/TCO claims, with benefits asserted without baselines, measurement, or enterprise impact.
sub_criteria: Are AI initiatives selected because they are fashionable, visible, or technically interesting?
Are savings, productivity, ROI, TCO, or efficiency claims made without baseline and post-measurement?
Are successful pilots celebrated without enterprise-level impact?

criteria.title: Rigid Gatekeeping Governance
criteria.description: AI governance slows flow without improving safety, leaving teams unclear how to proceed or incentivizing shadow AI.
sub_criteria: Does governance act as a separate hurdle that slows flow without improving safety?
Are teams unclear how to proceed safely, so they bypass governance or create shadow AI?
Are governance decisions disconnected from business impact, architecture, and operational reality?

criteria.title: Unclassified Risk & Ambiguous Accountability
criteria.description: AI use cases launch without risk classification, accountable owners, human override, escalation, or appeal mechanisms.
sub_criteria: Are AI use cases launched without risk classification?
Is it unclear who is accountable when an AI-assisted decision causes harm or failure?
Are human override, appeal, fallback, or escalation mechanisms missing?

criteria.title: AI Investment Drift
criteria.description: The AI portfolio grows without capacity, readiness, value proof, learning logic, or willingness to stop weak initiatives.
sub_criteria: Does the AI backlog grow without capacity, architectural readiness, or value proof?
Are weak initiatives kept alive because of sunk cost, politics, or executive enthusiasm?
Are investments focused on platform build-out without near-term capability validation?

criteria.title: Ownerless Data & Context Loss
criteria.description: Data ownership is centralized, undefined, or detached from business meaning, leaving AI teams to guess context.
sub_criteria: Is data ownership centralized in IT or undefined, causing business context to disappear?
Are AI teams forced to interpret datasets without domain meaning?
Do data issues stall AI use cases because nobody owns correction or interpretation?

criteria.title: Raw Data Without Meaning
criteria.description: AI systems receive available raw data without semantic richness, service context, process linkage, operational conditions, or decision relevance.
sub_criteria: Is data collected because it is available rather than because it drives decisions?
Do AI models receive raw signals without business, process, or operational context?
Are outputs unreliable because the model lacks the why-this-data-matters layer and service-domain meaning?

criteria.title: Data Swamp & Broken Lineage
criteria.description: AI outputs rely on stale copies, undocumented transformations, unknown origins, and unprovable data quality.
sub_criteria: Are AI outputs based on data whose origin, version, or quality cannot be proven?
Are stale copies, manual files, or undocumented transformations used in AI workflows?
Are data quality failures discovered only after model failure or business escalation?

criteria.title: Data Leakage & Over-Broad Access
criteria.description: AI tools access sensitive data with unclear purpose, logging, approval, retention, or boundary controls.
sub_criteria: Can AI tools access sensitive data without clear purpose, logging, or approval?
Are copies of data moved into experimentation environments without lifecycle control?
Are privacy and security controls added late instead of being designed into the data flow?

criteria.title: Ad Hoc Retrieval & Duplicate Knowledge Stores
criteria.description: Teams create stale, incomplete, duplicate, or unowned RAG, embedding, feature, and knowledge stores.
sub_criteria: Does each AI team create its own embeddings, indexes, or knowledge base without ownership?
Are RAG systems using stale, incomplete, or unverified source material?
Are retrieval failures treated as model failures instead of data-access architecture failures?

criteria.title: AI Ideas Detached from Business Architecture
criteria.description: AI use cases are listed without linkage to service catalog, capability map, value stream, service-area ownership, data domain, or dependency structure.
sub_criteria: Are AI use cases listed without connection to service catalog or capability map?
Is it unclear which service area owns the AI-enabled change?
Are service, platform, data, and brownfield dependencies discovered only during implementation?

criteria.title: Spot Optimization & Silo Automation
criteria.description: AI speeds isolated tasks while increasing downstream rework, coordination, or poor customer/service flow.
sub_criteria: Is AI applied to isolated tasks without understanding the surrounding flow?
Does automation speed up one step while increasing downstream rework or coordination?
Are customer experience and end-to-end flow ignored in AI design?

criteria.title: Untraceable AI Build Logic
criteria.description: AI components are built without clear linkage to capability, customer need, data source, platform dependency, or value outcome.
sub_criteria: Are teams building AI components without clear linkage to business capability or customer need?
Are requirements vague, unstable, or tool-led?
Is there no traceability between AI feature, data source, platform dependency, and value outcome?

criteria.title: Disconnected AI Project Teams
criteria.description: AI teams are separated from service areas and ownership disappears after pilots, vendors, or temporary projects.
sub_criteria: Are AI teams separate from the service areas that need to own the outcome?
Are business, data science, application, and platform work split into sequential handoffs?
Does ownership disappear after pilot completion or vendor delivery?

criteria.title: Big-Bang AI Transformation
criteria.description: AI is scaled broadly before Kickstart learning proves service readiness, architecture, data ownership, safety, and operating model patterns.
sub_criteria: Is AI rollout scaled broadly before business architecture, data ownership, and operating model are ready?
Are pilot learnings not converted into reusable patterns, playbooks, guardrails, or absorption-readiness evidence?
Does every service area repeat the same mistakes independently?
